payload.name: Preserve image-sharing action from provenance references
payload.description: When extracting memories from a message where the speaker credits or describes a picture/image they shared (e.g., 'That picture is from...', 'This was made by...'), use this Skill to record the sharing event and its source.
content: If a user message refers to a previously shared picture or image and states its creator/provenance (e.g., 'That picture is from X'), extract an event memory that the user shared that picture, including the creator/source as a detail.

Do not convert the picture's source into ownership of a physical themed object (e.g., a bookshelf or decoration) unless the message explicitly states the user owns such an object; do not infer physical objects from figurative praise.

During CRUD, if an existing memory records an inferred ownership but the evidence only supports a sharing event, ADD the sharing event or UPDATE the memory to include the sharing action so the shared picture's provenance is not lost.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often drops the sharing action when a user credits a picture they shared (e.g., 'That picture is from X'), instead hallucinating an ownership event about a themed physical object. This Skill applies when a message references a shared image and states its provenance, and instructs extracting the picture-sharing event with its source while avoiding inferred physical-object ownership. It does not apply when the user explicitly states they own an item, where an ownership/possession memory remains correct.

payload.name: Extract implicit photo-sharing from 'Here are' cues
payload.description: When a message uses 'Here are/is' to present physical items the speaker made or has, without naming a photo, extract that the speaker shared a photo of those items.
content: During extraction, if a speaker presents physical items with 'Here are/is' (e.g., 'Here are some bowls I made') and no photo/picture word appears, include a memory/event that the speaker shared a photo of those items, alongside facts about making/possession.
Do not apply this when 'Here are/is' introduces abstract content (steps, thoughts, lists) or when the message already explicitly mentions sharing a photo; rely on the base policy in those cases.

candidates.solves: Candidates extracted from messages where a speaker says 'Here are ...' for tangible items they created often keep the creation fact but drop the displayed photo-sharing fact, making future 'shared a photo of' questions unanswerable. This Skill applies when future questions ask what someone shared a photo of and the evidence contains a deictic presentation of physical objects. It must not apply to 'Here are' phrases about abstract lists or already explicit photo mentions.
